title: Junta Fourier coefficient estimation
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, let $P\subseteq[n]$, and fix signs on the coordinates in $P$. Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let the rational failure parameter $\eta$ satisfy $0<\eta\le 1/2$, and choose any Fourier index $S$ in the low-degree family on the remaining coordinates, whose members have size at most $\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor$. For the uniform batch of free-coordinate inputs of the sample size specified by the low-degree junta coefficient estimator, the probability that its empirical estimate of the $S$-th Fourier coefficient of the restricted function differs from the true coefficient by at least $1/(3\cdot 2^k)$ is at most the estimator's confidence parameter (the quarter-failure parameter divided by the size of that Fourier family).
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a subset of $[n]$ and fixed signs are assigned on $P$
$S$ belongs to the specified low-degree Fourier family
caveat: The sample size and confidence are defined through several upstream formulas; the statement summarizes those derived quantities rather than expanding the full sample-count formula.
